Providers stringify array/object tool params, so every args-mode call reported 'Provide exactly one input mode' (P28 prepareArguments); prompt-surface slimming (guide-gate companion, Round-2 lineage — current shape maintained in playbook.js, see PATCHES.md).
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE: wave21 filled the parameter schema. Another agent session read this guide in full and still could not make a single successful call — args died with "args is not iterable", job with "job.steps must be a non-empty array" while P28 was fine. Cause: every parameter was declared {} so the model was told the parameter exists and nothing else; it guessed args as an array-of-arrays because that is what stdin looks like for batch, then read the guide, concluded the patch was clobbered, and reported a bug that did not exist. Now each parameter carries a type and a description, and every mode-object admits string|object because this host stringifies object params.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wave-7 numeric-token coercion was unreachable: the Pi host validates the `stdin` tool param as an array-of-string-arrays before execute() runs, so [["mouse","move",489,119]] never reaches this file on this host. Dead code that misrepresented the contract was deleted; the error still names the offending token type.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30, second pass. The host wraps EVERY array element recursively: [["get","url"],["get","title"]] arrives as [{item:[{item:"get"},{item:"url"}]},{item:[{item:"get"},{item:"title"}]}]. Unwrapping only the outer level then failed with "token 0 must be a string (got object)", which is what exposed the inner level. The envelope is now stripped at every depth and the count is reported as itemEnvelopesStripped. Safety is structural, not a guess: batch validation requires every token to be a string, so no object can appear in a batch that would have validated, making the strip provably a no-op on every input that already worked. Three wrong theories preceded this: comma-joining, flattening, and outer-envelope-only.

entries.upstreamDefect: No structural guard existed against local-patch clobbering: an update could overwrite the 28 hand-applied patches and the wrapper would keep spawning silently (pre-spawn verifyPatchLedger gate).

The click-dispatch probe counted EVERY trusted event that reached the target equally, so a bare pointerdown satisfied it. Any target that was re-rendered or moved between mousedown and mouseup therefore read as a successful dispatch, hiding the single most common real-browser false success: upstream reports 'Clicked: @eN', the app does nothing.
entries.localFix: The probe now separates press events (pointerdown/mousedown) from terminal ones (pointerup/mouseup/click) and only a terminal event clears a miss. Press-without-terminal is reported as the distinct status press-observed-click-missing and named as such in the summary, so the caller is told the element was re-rendered or moved instead of receiving the generic no-event wording. No synthetic click is ever dispatched.

entries.upstreamDefect: Nothing: this file is new and local. The upstream agent-browser CLI exposes no raw CDP surface, and its command list belongs to a third-party binary the wrapper cannot extend. Yusuf's requirement was an agent able to drive the browser freely, so the wrapper needed a channel past the CLI's command vocabulary.
entries.localFix: The cdp input mode: normalise + compile a { session?, commands[{method,params?,artifact?}], artifactPath?, timeoutMs } payload with 8 validation rules, no I/O. Wired as a host-only kind so the wrapper's argv guards are skipped, matching vault/login/devServer.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30 (wave14b): Runtime.evaluate works after the attach handshake; multi-command ordering; artifact written; bogus method fails naming the method; Browser.getVersion falls back to the browser session; cdp+args rejected.

entries.upstreamDefect: Same gap as P-W14-cdp-mode, on the execution side: there was no way to speak CDP to the already-running browser. The CLI does expose `get cdp-url`, so the endpoint is reachable through the normal spawn pipeline, but nothing consumed it.
entries.localFix: Resolves the endpoint via the injected dispatch (get cdp-url, so redaction and the ledger still apply), opens one WebSocket from the Node 22 global, sends the commands sequentially on one connection, and returns per-command results in order. Heavy payloads go to artifactPath instead of inline. webSocketImpl is injectable so the offline test never opens a socket. No new dependency.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30 (wave14b): attach handshake, artifact on disk, -32601 browser-session fallback, and the 35/35 no-regression after the wave17 abort refactor. The ABORT PATH ITSELF is offline-verified only - it cannot be triggered from the tool interface without cancelling the call from outside. wave17 abort semantics remain offline-verified only.

entries.summary: wave15: refuse an unrecognized upstream flag before the spawn, with a near-miss suggestion
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30: --nonsense-flag refused instantly naming the flag; --new-tabs produced "Did you mean --new-tab?"; real short and long flags (snapshot -i, --quiet, --session) all still work.
entries.upstreamDefect: agent-browser 0.37.0 ignores a flag it does not recognise instead of refusing it, so a mistyped flag produced no error at all: the spawn went out, nothing consumed the flag, and the call sat until the wrapper's 35s watchdog fired and reported 'timeout'. That is the worst possible answer twice over - it burns 35 seconds and it names the wrong cause, so a model repeats the same typo. The wrapper already carries the full upstream flag surface in this file, so the fix is a lookup rather than a new vocabulary.

agent-browser's `find` takes the FIRST match and offers no visibility filter, so it lands on hidden 0x0 duplicates - `find text "Run"` once clicked a hidden duplicate instead of the real 71x32 button. Measured consequence: 169 of 435 eval --stdin calls in the 14 use-case sweep (39%) were the model re-deriving the same candidate walk in JavaScript by hand, precisely because `find` could not be trusted. The upstream CLI cannot be changed from here, but the wrapper can own the JavaScript, so `act` generates it once.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30: on a real fixture, considered 6 / visible 5 / matched 1 proved the visibility filter drops a display:none duplicate; two visible "Publish" returned status ambiguous with both rects and NO clicked flag; a later read proved log stayed "-" so the refusal was real; read+limit reported truncated with totalChars; role:link matched a bare <a>. The click was verified through the page state (DETAILS-CLICKED), not the tool's own "clicked": true. Known scope limit found live: the candidate selector covers interactive elements only, so act cannot read a plain <div>.

entries.upstreamDefect: Not an upstream defect - a wrapper-local default that was never measured. DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_DELTA_MIN_LINES was 2000, which only fires on the 4000+ node class, so an ordinary large page (github: 732 rendered lines, ~24k chars, ~6k tokens) re-rendered in full on every snapshot. Measured 2026-09-30 with the cdp escape hatch: tokopedia 253 lines, github 732, wikipedia 3238. Lowered to 600. The file was also previously un-ledgered, so drift in it was invisible to the integrity check.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30. Both branches proven in a real browser: wikipedia 547 interactive lines > 400 -> "Delta snapshot (vs previous): 0 refs changed (547 total)", 62,223 bytes -> 128 (486x); github 141 lines < 400 -> correctly stays full. Key insight: on the interactive snapshot string one line is one ref, so this is a ref-count threshold. Two earlier tunings (600 on full-snapshot counts, 426/1600 on artifact-wide string counts) were both wrong; only countRenderedSnapshotLines(artifact.snapshot) matches the gate.

entries.upstreamDefect: Not an upstream defect - a local usability defect. The slim schema declared every parameter as an empty object, so the model was told a parameter exists with no type, shape or description. Since the model reads the schema before it reads the docs, the docs cannot fix a wrong guess made from the schema: an agent that read all 2,242 lines still failed every call. Fixed by declaring a type and a one-line description per parameter, and by allowing string on every mode-object since this host re-coerces object params to strings. tests-v2/wave21-tool-schema.mjs asserts this against the real tool definition a host receives, not against source text; a source match would pass while the host kept getting {}.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30; the final shape was found by testing both wrong declarations. This harness sends args as an ARRAY (delivered wrapped in {item:[...]}) and stdin as a STRING (delivered intact), shown verbatim in the host's own validation error. So the two are declared differently: args = string|array WITH items (an array type without items is invalid JSON Schema 6.4.1 and left the runner's reconstruction undefined); stdin = string ONLY, because an array-declared stdin makes the host append a stray ']' to the string and reject it with 'trailing characters at line 1 column 32'. Both wrong declarations were live-tested: string-only args failed every call ('args: must be string'), array stdin failed with the trailing-closer error. The {item:...} envelope is stripped in code for BOTH argv and batch stdin, and the parser still accepts a real array for stdin.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local diagnostics, not an upstream defect. Proven live on a real 65-question exam: (1) the host comma-joins a nested array stdin param, so a correct [[..],[..]] arrives as an array of strings, and the old error blamed 'step 0 must be a non-empty array' - the shape, never the cause, so the caller could not find the JSON-string fix on its own. (2) batch steps run back-to-back, so a click that navigates followed by a step targeting an element that only exists on the new page reports 'Element not found' and the caller naturally concludes the selector is wrong; the failing step is correct and the missing wait is the bug. The comma is the discriminator for (1) so a hand-built mistake is never blamed on the host, and the page-change check reads the existing command taxonomy rather than a hand-kept list, because a first attempt matching only 'click' missed 'open'.
entries.verifiedLive: SCOPE CORRECTED and batch RETIRED AS A CALLER COMMAND 2026-09-30. Removing batch outright would have been wrong: job, checkpoint restore, debug, login-flow and lookups all compile DOWN to a batch, and their stdin is built inside the wrapper in JS rather than passed as a tool parameter, so the host never reshapes it. Checkpoint restore is live-verified working. The host's reshaping is specific to the caller-supplied stdin parameter on the batch command, so only that entry point is refused, naming eval --stdin as the route that works. The first version of the guard took job down with it, because the skip list for compiler-generated args omitted compiledGeneratedBatch while job compiles to exactly the argv being rejected; the regression and both sabotages are now locked in tests-v2/wave22-batch-retired.mjs. Also corrected: an earlier guide said stdin was broken generally, which was wrong - eval --stdin with a plain string is verified working and is the recommended multi-step primitive.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local policy, not an upstream defect. The host reshapes the caller-supplied stdin tool parameter for the batch command into an array of string arrays before the tool body runs, so batch steps never arrive intact and no wrapper repair is reachable. batch is therefore refused as a caller command, with eval --stdin named as the replacement. batch is NOT removed: job, checkpoint, debug, login-flow and lookups compile down to it with stdin built in-wrapper, and those work.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30: a caller batch with two steps is now refused with the message naming eval --stdin, instead of the host's cryptic 'trailing characters at line 1 column 32'. the guard is offline-verified and sabotage-verified three ways Confirmed the retirement harms nothing downstream: checkpoint save+restore ran a full 4-step batch (state load, open <origin>, get url, snapshot) with every step succeeding, which is the W19 open-origin fix working end to end.

entries.upstreamDefect: Upstream host bug, repaired locally. This Pi build stringifies every tool parameter (earendil-works/pi#4226) and its runner wraps a NESTED array parameter in {item: ...} (hermes-agent#104803), so a job whose `steps` is an array of objects arrives wrapped and each step reads as a bare string, producing the misleading 'job.steps must be a non-empty array' for a payload that is correct. Same host class as the caller-batch breakage, reaching the tool through the job object instead. A job step is always an object carrying an `action`, so {item: ...} can never be a legitimate step and the strip is a no-op on any job that already worked.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30. The exact job that failed with 'job.steps must be a non-empty array' now runs both steps to completion against a real page: step 1 snapshot -i returned 1628 refs, step 2 wait --url skillbuilder.aws resolved. This also proves job's internal batch runs, which is the half of the earlier reasoning that was wrong: the host mangles only what crosses the stdin tool-parameter boundary, and job builds that stdin in wrapper JS (input-plan.js:413 takes compiledJob.stdin, never params.stdin, and a guard refuses a caller-supplied stdin alongside job). The guide's earlier claim that job failed for the same reason as batch is falsified and has been corrected. Offline: 29/29, 25 ledgered files matching. | wave23: the predicate moved to shared.js because five call sites hit this same host defect, and job.js's local copy is gone; the test asserts no mode re-declares it.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local defect, not an upstream one. compileAgentBrowserSourceLookup accepted a `session` field, never read it, and never validated it: the compiled argv was a bare ["batch"] with no --session, so a lookup naming a session silently ran against the root session instead. networkSourceLookup in the same file already threaded session correctly, so the two had drifted apart.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30. Before the fix, sourceLookup on session ultron1 reported 'Element not found' on both steps while its next-action named the ROOT session. After the fix, the same call returns step 1 succeeded (origin = the ultron1 AWS summary page) and step 2 succeeded returning the banner text that exists only in that session. The session mismatch was the whole bug.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local defect, not an upstream one. compileAgentBrowserDebug never handled `session` at all — the field was absent from the compiler and argv was a bare ["batch","--bail"] — so a devtools report requested for a named session ran against the root session. Same class as the sourceLookup defect fixed earlier in this wave. Audited the whole input-modes directory: debug was the only remaining mode that both builds argv and accepts a session without threading it. job, act, networkSourceLookup and login (via the P27 runtime dispatch wrapper) were already correct.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30 for the session threading: the exact checkConsole call that reported 'get url = about:blank' and 'get title = empty' now reports the real ultron1 URL and title 'AWS Skill Builder', with 110 console messages instead of 'none'. SECOND defect found while testing that fix: debug emitted its eval rows before its console/errors/network rows, and an eval marks the page unverified for the rest of the batch, so every evidence row after the first was refused — 'debug actionable' with an expectedSelector could not run at all while checkConsole worked, which made it look like a guard problem. The order is now evidence-then-assertions, with a get url re-verify between assertions because a second eval in one batch is refused too (expectedText:[a,b] could not run). The step-order fix is offline-verified and awaits a restart; the session threading is live-verified.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local ordering defect against a correct upstream-style guard. The page-target guard treats an eval as an unverified page transition, which is right, but compileAgentBrowserDebug emitted its assertion rows (expectedText / expectedSelector / evalExpression) BEFORE its evidence rows (console, errors, network requests, snapshot), so every evidence row after the first eval was refused. A second eval in the same batch is refused too, so multi-assertion calls could not run at all. Fixed by emitting evidence first and assertions last, with a get url re-verify between assertions. The reverify rows are deliberately not eval rows: the report consumes eval rows through a plan-order cursor, so an extra eval would shift every verdict onto the wrong check.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30. `debug actionable` with an expectedSelector, which previously could not run at all ('The active page became unverified'), now completes 6 steps: get url, get title, console, errors, network requests, and the assertion eval. The step-order fix works. Separately, a THIRD debug defect surfaced while verifying it — see P-W22-debug-verdict.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local defect against a correct analyzer. analyzeDebugPresetResults expects the CHECKS half of a compiled debug, but process-output.js passed the whole compiled object. The analyzer reads input.expectedText / expectedSelector / evalExpression directly and those live one level down under `.checks`, so getExpectedEvalRoles returned an empty list and no eval row was ever assigned a role. One call site, one property access.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED after restart 2026-09-30, all four directions on a real page. PASS text: page contains 'Halo Dunia', eval row returns true, report says 'no failures detected' with expectedTextChecked 1. FAIL text: 'TIDAK-ADA-INI' -> eval returns false, report says 'expected text not found'. FAIL selector: '#tidak-ada' -> eval returns false, report says 'expected selector not visible'. PASS selector: '#ada-di-halaman' -> eval returns true, report says 'no failures detected'. Two assertions in one call also work, and the reverify row is visible as step 7 letting the second eval run: 8 steps, text passed and selector failed, each reported separately and correctly. Before this chain the same calls said 'no failures detected' for a page missing the text, then 'expected text not found' for a page that demonstrably contained it; both were lies and the intermediate one was mine.

entries.upstreamDefect: Upstream host defect with five call sites, one shared repair. This Pi build serialises every tool parameter to a string (earendil-works/pi#4226) and its runner wraps a NESTED array parameter in {item: [...]} (hermes-agent#104803). Confirmed live for stdin/batch (retired), job.steps, debug.expectedText and cdp.commands. Each had been treated as an unrelated bug; the shared definition in input-modes/shared.js is what makes the fifth one findable.
entries.verifiedLive: PARTIALLY LIVE-VERIFIED. Host behaviour proved live for debug.expectedText, cdp.commands and job.steps[].values; the repairs are offline-verified and await a restart. Reviewer-lane findings, all CONFIRMED before fixing: (a) FOUR more caller-array sites had the same defect and were being fixed one at a time — qa.expectedText, select values, the electron string-array fields, vault.fill.fields — all now healed; (b) the wave23 comment claimed electron was healed while electron.js never imported the helper and the test iterated only three files while printing 'all five array sites healed' — that was my own overclaim and both the comment and the test scope are corrected, and the test now asserts every site the comment names; (c) analyzeNetworkSourceLookupResults reported 'found no failed requests' when the batch returned no rows at all, i.e. nothing inspected reported as a clean network — now a distinct no-results status, with the boundary drawn at 'a network requests result always carries a requests array', so an upstream that ran and found nothing still reports honestly. Also added unwrapItemEnvelopeDeep after live observation of a payload wrapped twice, which a single-level strip does not survive; bounded, and still positional so free-form CDP params are untouched. SECOND REVIEW ROUND, same wave. A reviewer lane reported networkBody maxChars being silently clamped; confirmed by grep BEFORE fixing and it is real, with the numbers in the report wrong: clampedFrom was computed, carried and then READ NOWHERE (all four occurrences inside the normalizer), so a caller asking for 99999 got 40000 and was told nothing. Now stated in the note, including the urlFilter branch. The same report claimed direction was dropped — it is not; it is preserved on the value and consumed by extractNetworkBodies. Both are asserted in the test so they are settled rather than merely re-rejected. 40000 is the ceiling and 4000 the default, not a 40000-truncates-to-4000 bug.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local. Two silent-lying paths found by a reviewer fan-out: (1) networkBody maxChars above the ceiling was clamped and clampedFrom computed, carried and never read, so the truncation was invisible; (2) analyzeNetworkSourceLookupResults reported "found no failed requests" when the batch returned no rows at all, i.e. nothing inspected read as a clean network. The boundary for (2) is that a network requests result that actually ran always carries a requests array, so a populated one is a real answer even when empty.
entries.verifiedLive: PARTIALLY LIVE-VERIFIED. The networkSourceLookup no-results half is live-verified in the direction above. The networkBody clamp half: the clamp is reached and EXECUTES — a maxChars of 99999 passes validation instead of being refused, which is what the fix depends on, and the previous build refused it. The rendered clamp sentence is NOT observable on this host because `network request <id>` returns 'Request not found' for every id that `network requests` just listed, so no body read ever succeeds; the build does not retain body detail, which is exactly what the note anticipates. A number sent inside a mode object is stringified by the host transport and correctly rejected as 'must be a positive integer'; the JSON-string form of the whole object passes the number through untouched, which is the only form in which a numeric maxChars can arrive at all.

entries.upstreamDefect: Wrapper-local, three distinct silent-lying paths found by the remaining reviewer lanes and each CONFIRMED by running it before the fix. (1) The qa preset path still carried the pre-fix defect class that debug was corrected for in wave22: an empty expectedText compiled into a preset that asserted nothing and reported "QA preset passed"; a preset whose batch returned no rows produced no verdict at all yet the run stayed succeeded; and a wait --fn row whose verdict could not be read fell through to return true, scoring an unreadable predicate as a PASS. All three now report absent or unreadable as neither pass nor fail, matching the debug.js contract. (2) isBrowserIndependentRead tested !== undefined, and null !== undefined, so every MALFORMED read was classified as a browser-independent read — the exact opposite of the comment on that function — which skipped the managed-session ownership check and page-target validation for a call the wrapper already knew was malformed. (3) applyNetworkRouteRecords returned undefined for a route command with no pattern, which the caller turns into "erase every route for this session", after which buildNetworkRouteDiagnostics returned undefined and the unfulfilled/CORS/pending diagnostics stopped firing with no message; it also persisted a flag as a URL pattern (network route --abort stored {pattern:"--abort"}). Malformed route commands are now no-ops. Separately, resetDiagnosticsBufferState had ZERO callers in dist/, so a closed session kept its dedup buffer and a browser reopened under the same name had brand-new rows reported as already-reported.
entries.verifiedLive: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-30 after a restart, in the directions a live browser can actually reach. qa PASSING: reported 'QA preset passed' with 'Checks run: ... text x1 ...', so the assertion really executed. qa FAILING: reported 'QA preset failed: wait failed; expected text not found: "TIDAK-ADA-..."' naming the text. qa EMPTY expectedText: refused live with 'qa.expectedText must be a non-empty string or array of non-empty strings when provided.' networkSourceLookup: on a real page whose batch succeeded and returned 2 populated requests, it reported 'found no failed requests' as a genuine clean result — the boundary the fix drew is the right one, because a populated requests array is a real answer. NOT REACHABLE LIVE, and deliberately not claimed: the qa no-rows and unreadable-verdict paths need a batch that returns nothing or a row whose verdict cannot be read, and no real page produced one. The read null-sentinel fix is honest only about classification: the malformed read is now rejected upstream with a proper usage error, but that error is IDENTICAL before and after the fix; what changed is that the managed-session ownership check and page-target validation now run, which is not observable from the call result. Separately re-confirmed live: a 2-step job with a doubly-enveloped steps array runs both steps and reports each outcome, and the session is threaded into nextActions. An assertText timeout on example.com was investigated and is NOT a defect — wait --text reads body text while example.com keeps 'Example Domain' only in its <title>; the same assertText passes on text that is in the body and fails on text that is absent.
